## The question {#sec-question}

Nine Gates is the wait `1112345678999`: drawing any of the nine ranks completes
four melds and a pair. We use the general framework of @xue-zhong-2026, allowing
$3n$ ranks, a meld count $m$, and a physical copy cap $q$ to vary independently.
A meld is either three identical ranks or three consecutive ranks.

Write $c_i$ for the multiplicity of paper rank $i$, numbered from $1$ to $3n$.
A full-sided wait has $3m+1$ tiles and wins after every possible draw.
It is **live** when every draw also respects the physical copy cap:

$$
c_i+1\le q\qquad(1\le i\le 3n).
$$ {#eq-live-cap}

The eight-family theorem classifies full-sided waits at $m=n+1$.
Here we ask a coarser question: **which meld counts can occur at all?**
We do not attempt to count or classify every hand at a given meld count.

## The exact interval with four copies {#sec-interval}

::: {#thm-live-interval}
## Existence interval

For natural numbers $n,m$, there is a live full-sided wait on $3n$ ranks
with $m$ melds and physical copy cap four if and only if

$$
n<m<3n.
$$
:::

For $n=1$, the only possible meld count is $m=2$.
For ordinary nine-rank Mahjong ($n=3$), the possible counts are $4,5,6,7,8$.
These are existence statements, not claims about how many waits there are.

### Why these bounds are necessary

The structural class-size bounds give $m>n$
[@xue-zhong-2026, Proposition 5.7]. The other inequality is immediate from
liveness: @eq-live-cap gives $c_i\le3$, hence

$$
3m+1=\sum_{i=1}^{3n}c_i\le9n,
$$

and therefore $m<3n$.
More generally, any live full-sided wait satisfies $m<n(q-1)$.

### Filling every gap

Start with the generalized Nine Gates hand

$$
A_n=(3,\underbrace{1,\ldots,1}_{3n-2},3),
$$

which has $n+1$ melds. Adding any sequence preserves full-sidedness:
a decomposition for each old winning draw can simply include the extra sequence.

Suppose $n<m<3n$. Put

$$
\begin{aligned}
k&=m-(n+1),\\
a&=\min(k,n-1),\\
b&=k-a.
\end{aligned}
$$

Then $a+b=k$ and $0\le a,b\le n-1$.
Add one layer of $a$ disjoint sequences covering the first $3a$ interior ranks,
and another layer of $b$ disjoint sequences covering the first $3b$ interior ranks.
Each interior multiplicity increases by at most two, and the boundary
multiplicities stay at three. Thus the resulting hand is still live under
cap four, and its meld count is exactly $n+1+a+b=m$.
This proves @thm-live-interval.

::: {#tbl-six-ranks}

+-------+-------+--------------------------+
| $n$   | $m$   | A constructed live wait  |
+=======+=======+==========================+
| $2$   | $3$   | $(3,1,1,1,1,3)$          |
+-------+-------+--------------------------+
| $2$   | $4$   | $(3,2,2,2,1,3)$          |
+-------+-------+--------------------------+
| $2$   | $5$   | $(3,3,3,3,1,3)$          |
+-------+-------+--------------------------+

All admissible meld counts at order two, using the same two-layer construction.
:::

@tbl-six-ranks illustrates the construction. @fig-live-region shows its
parameter range and an extremal nine-rank hand.

```{python}
#| label: fig-live-region
#| fig-cap: "Left: the admissible integer pairs (n,m) under copy cap four. Right: an extremal nine-rank hand with eight melds. The dots plot the proved interval, not an enumeration of candidate hands."

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9, 3.7), layout="constrained")
fig.patch.set_facecolor("white")

ax = axes[0]
xs = np.linspace(0.8, 7.2, 100)
ax.fill_between(xs, xs, 3 * xs, color="#407b9f", alpha=0.10)
ax.plot(xs, xs, "--", color="#8c4a53", linewidth=1, label=r"$m=n$")
ax.plot(xs, 3 * xs, "--", color="#4e7291", linewidth=1, label=r"$m=3n$")
for n in range(1, 8):
    counts = np.arange(n + 1, 3 * n)
    ax.scatter(np.full(len(counts), n), counts, s=17, color="#285c79", zorder=3)
ax.set(xlabel=r"order $n$", ylabel=r"meld count $m$", xlim=(0.6, 7.4), ylim=(0, 22))
ax.set_xticks(range(1, 8))
ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
ax.grid(alpha=0.12)
ax.set_title(r"$n<m<3n$", fontsize=11)

ax = axes[1]
hand = np.array([3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 1, 3])
colors = ["#7297a7"] * 9
colors[7] = "#b76668"
ax.bar(np.arange(1, 10), hand, color=colors, width=0.68)
ax.axhline(3, color="#59636b", linestyle="--", linewidth=0.8)
ax.set(xlabel="paper rank", ylabel="multiplicity before drawing", ylim=(0, 3.8))
ax.set_xticks(range(1, 10))
ax.set_yticks(range(4))
ax.set_title(r"$n=3,\quad m=8$", fontsize=11)
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
plt.show()
```

::: {#cor-largest-live}
## Largest live meld count

At every positive order $n$, the largest live meld count under cap four is
$3n-1$. It is attained by the hand with three copies of each rank except a
single copy of the penultimate rank.
:::

## Why four physical copies are the minimum {#sec-minimum-cap}

::: {#prp-three-copies}
## A triple is unavoidable

Every full-sided wait contains at least three copies of some rank,
regardless of its order or meld count. Consequently every live full-sided wait
requires $q\ge4$.
:::

Here is a short class-size argument. Group ranks by their residues modulo three,
and let $C_R$ be the total multiplicity in residue class $R$.
Every sequence contributes one tile to each class; a triplet contributes
three tiles to just one class.

The draw-pair congruence singles out a fixed class $S$: a draw in $S$ uses a pair
in $S$, while a draw in either other class uses a pair in the remaining class
[@xue-zhong-2026, Proposition 4.2 and Definition 4.3].

::: {.proof}

Suppose all original multiplicities are at most two. After drawing rank $i$
and removing a pair, only rank $i$ can have multiplicity at least three.
Thus every triplet in a winning decomposition must lie at the drawn rank.
Any other class consists entirely of sequences and has no larger class size
than the drawn class.

First draw in $S$. Removing the pair reduces the net size of $S$ by one,
so for either nonfixed class $T$ we obtain $C_T\le C_S-1$.
Now draw in the other nonfixed class and remove a pair from $T$.
The class $S$ has no triplets, giving $C_S\le C_T-2$.
The two inequalities contradict each other.

Therefore some rank has multiplicity at least three. A live draw at that rank
requires at least four physical copies, as claimed in @prp-three-copies.
:::

The bound is attained: $A_n$ is live with four physical copies at every positive
order. Thus the minimum copy cap is exactly four.
